name: Ethos Invest
tagline: Invest in line with your values, without the jargon
about: Ethos Invest helps beginners invest by their values: a values screen you can actually apply, greenwash checks on fund marketing, a test of whether a fund's holdings pass your screen, a plan for switching your bank and pension, and plain-English answers to the hard questions.
persona: You are an ethical-investing educator: neutral on which values are right, rigorous about fees and tracking difference, sceptical of marketing labels, and never recommending specific securities.

onboarding.title: Money that matches your values
onboarding.subtitle: Your priorities set the screen; we'll keep the finance plain.
bullets: A values screen you can apply

tools.title: Build my values screen
tools.subtitle: Exclusions, inclusions, dealbreakers

inputs.label: In your own words
inputs.placeholder: no fossil fuels or weapons, OK with banks if they lend to renewables, prefer companies paying a living wage

tools.prompt: Turn '{values}' plus the profile's priorities into an investable screen: table (Theme | Exclude | Tolerate with limits | Actively seek), kv (screening approach that fits: negative, best-in-class, impact or engagement), bullets on the trade-offs (diversification, fees, tracking difference), and a callout on values that are hard to screen for in practice and why.

tools.title: Greenwash check
tools.subtitle: Photo or paste → what it really commits to

inputs.label: Photo or screenshot of the fund page, label or advert

tools.prompt: Check the fund marketing from the photo and/or: {text} against the profile's priorities. Table (Claim made | What it actually commits to | Greenwash risk low/med/high | Question to ask), kv (labelling approach: exclusion, best-in-class, impact, engagement or 'ESG integration' only; exclusions actually listed; overall greenwash score out of 10), bullets on the weasel words spotted, and a callout on why 'ESG integration' alone rarely changes what a fund holds.

tools.title: Does it pass my screen?
tools.subtitle: Top holdings → what clashes with your values
tools.prompt: Test the holdings of '{fund}': {holdings} against the profile's priorities. Table (Holding | Weight | Passes? yes / grey / no | Concern | Where to verify), kv (weight that fails, weight in a grey area, biggest single conflict, verdict: keep / tolerate / look elsewhere), bullets on the options (accept, engage via the provider, choose a screened alternative), and a callout that holdings lists are snapshots and sector labels hide subsidiaries.

tools.title: Move my bank & pension
tools.subtitle: Where your money already sits

inputs.label: Current bank and pension
inputs.placeholder: high-street bank current account, workplace pension in the default fund

tools.prompt: For: {current} in the profile region — steps to check where the pension default is invested and how to switch to an ethical option within the same scheme, a checklist for switching banks with minimal disruption, a table (Money pot | How to check its ethics | Effort | Impact), and a callout on not losing employer contributions, guarantees or protection when moving.

tools.title: Hard questions
tools.subtitle: Does it even work? Do I lose returns?

inputs.label: Question
options: Does ethical investing actually change anything?

tools.prompt: Answer '{question}' for a beginner in the profile region: text with the balanced evidence in plain English, bullets of the strongest points on each side, kv (what the evidence says, what's uncertain, what you can control), and a quote with a one-sentence takeaway.

disclaimer: Educational only, not financial advice; investments can fall in value, and you should consider a regulated adviser before acting.
